newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London dip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London dip on profit-taking.

text.p: Japanese shares trading in London were generally lower on Thursday with profit-taking in autos and banks featuring in otherwise quiet trade, dealers said.
"It's extremely quiet," said one senior trader. "But there is definite selling interest in some motors and banks."

London's Nikkei/Ise 50 index was down 13.51 points or 0.92 percent at 1,455.13 by 1415 GMT. Tokyo's 225 share average was hit by profit-taking on Thursday to end down 167.1 points or 0.78 percent at 21,331.50.
"Tokyo will probably be down another 100 points tomorrow," the trader said. "There's not enough buying interest left."
"People were trying to hold out for the 22,000 mark but they don't think it will get there now."
Among individual features in London dealers said Nissan, Honda and Toyota all suffered from follow-through selling after weakness in Tokyo.
"The motors were very weak in Japan after the dollar started to back off from 112 yen," one dealer said. "The profit-taking has carried on in London."
Nissan Motor slipped to 901 yen after a Tokyo close of 905 yen. Toyota Motor fell to 2,805 yen after finishing at 2,810 in Japan and Honda Motor was unchanged at 2,810 yen by 1430 GMT.
Dealers said weakness in some bank shares had also continued in London, in particular shares in Industrial Bank of Japan which fell to 2,382.5 yen after a Tokyo close of 2,4000.
